A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SeaS. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation, downstream detection and segmentation, and ablation results on MVTec AD and RGB images from MVTec 3D AD.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds VisA evaluations, detector-augmentation experiments, and further diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3.4 adds a normal-image output mode conditioned on the normal token alone, whereas v1 describes inference for abnormal image-mask pairs. The shared U-Net, UA prompts, DA/NA losses, mixed training and RMP architecture remain unchanged; this is a limited extension of the stated inference procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds VisA's 12 object categories alongside the retained MVTec datasets. Evaluation expands beyond anomaly-image generation and supervised segmentation to normal-image generation, anomaly replacement in synthesis-based detectors, and normal-image augmentation for unsupervised detectors.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates GLASS, PatchCore, MambaAD and Textual Inversion, and adds a DRAEM control using real training anomalies. CDC is removed from generation comparisons. DRAEM disappears as a synthesis source for the common segmentation networks but appears in new detector-augmentation comparisons. Earlier direct comparisons with RealNet, Shape-guided and FOD are removed.

E3.justification: v2 adds normal-image KID, anomaly-region IC-LPIPS, detector-augmentation protocols, lighting-specific training subsets and a real-anomaly DRAEM control. The RMP ablation baseline is revised from having no components to retaining coarse-mask supervision (v1 Table 5; v2 Table 6), without establishing a rerun. The principal few-shot split and generation-training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained token, loss, training-strategy and RMP ablations, v2 adds a fixed-prompt ablation, Textual Inversion comparison, lighting/background experiment, small-defect examples and t-SNE analysis of unseen-type generalization. Appendix A.13 adds a substantive control testing whether DRAEM gains exceed those obtained from access to the same real anomalies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run or seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, error bars or significance tests. Both present point estimates; averages across categories or models do not establish repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results, including VisA IS/IC-LPIPS of 1.27/0.26, normal-image KID and detector-augmentation outcomes. Retained MVTec AD generation and per-category segmentation scores are unchanged. Some MVTec 3D AD summaries change: average SeaS image-AUROC becomes 78.38 rather than 78.44, while DFMGAN image-AP changes from 82.83 to 83.83 despite unchanged component rows averaging 82.83.

T1.justification: The loss equations, attention formulation and Appendix A.2 multi-head-attention argument are retained. Explicit prompt indexing and added qualitative explanations do not introduce a substantive new mathematical definition, derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden SeaS from anomaly-image/mask generation supporting segmentation to unified generation of anomalies, normal images and masks. New central claims concern benefits for synthesis-based and unsupervised anomaly detectors, beyond the retained supervised-segmentation claims.

C2.justification: Appendices A.11–A.12 explicitly qualify generation of extremely subtle defects and distinguish unseen instances within known anomaly types from genuinely unseen types. v2 also explains Textual Inversion shortcomings and interprets detector-augmentation benefits. Earlier discussions emphasizing small supervised models outperforming larger unsupervised detectors are removed with their comparisons.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 newly specifies forward-diffusion t=1500 and 25 sampling steps, detector checkpoint sources, GLASS foreground-mask omissions and PatchCore preprocessing. These are additional disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to retained experiments. The per-stage resource/time breakdown is removed, while aggregate timings, core training hyperparameters and the code link remain.

R1.justification: The central positioning shifts from anomaly-only versus complete-image generation to one model serving anomaly, normal-image and mask generation, revising the contrasts with AnomalyDiffusion and DFMGAN. References supporting GLASS, MambaAD, PatchCore and VisA are added; references associated with RealNet, Shape-guided, FOD and FID are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions and conclusion are substantially rewritten around unified generation and broader downstream applications. Experimental discussion and appendices are reorganized, with MVTec 3D AD material redistributed and implementation, ablation and qualitative-result sections reordered.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. Tables consolidate datasets and image/pixel metrics; retained qualitative displays are merged, relocated or stripped of removed comparators. Figure 1 is redesigned, and normal-generation, feature-visualization, lighting, small-defect and t-SNE displays are added.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through defect-region diversity measurements, VisA evaluation and detector-augmentation experiments, including the real-anomaly control in Appendix A.13. Appendices A.11–A.12 also meaningfully constrain the generalization claims. These gains outweigh removed comparator/resource detail and limited reporting defects, including Table 4's inconsistent DFMGAN average. Uncertainty across runs remains unreported.
